policy: No claim may be presented above its recorded status and scope.

claims.statement: NeoEng D-Core is an independent product and not the implementation of the five-year engine program.
claims.scope: product governance baseline 1.11.0

claims.statement: The D-Core is the sole authority over canonical state in the homologated architecture.
claims.scope: official APIs and in-process integration contract

claims.statement: Canonical transitions are deterministic in the declared corpus on Linux x86_64 across GCC and Clang.
claims.scope: recorded GCC 14.2 and Clang 17 x86_64 corpus

claims.statement: x86_64 and ARM64 produce identical canonical state.
claims.scope: native cross-architecture campaign not executed

claims.statement: The runtime supports deterministic replay and retained historical reconstruction.
claims.scope: declared schemas and retained window

claims.statement: The runtime supports correction and deterministic resimulation across an eight-frame rollback window.
claims.scope: functional corpus; physical P1 latency qualification pending

claims.statement: Rollback p99 is at or below 2 ms on the contractual P1 profile.
claims.scope: P1 native campaign not executed

claims.statement: ECS maintenance is at or below 0.1 ms/frame with zero critical allocation on P1.
claims.scope: complete four-stream evidence pipeline is verified; native P1 p99 and zero-allocation qualification have not been executed or achieved

claims.statement: Time-travel navigation and semantic state diff are available for the current Body-based canonical schema.
claims.scope: bounded in-memory history and current schema

claims.statement: A requested comparison can locate the first observed divergence through stable hash, SHA-256, Merkle chunk and known semantic component.
claims.scope: current canonical Body schema; CS010 reference coordinator orchestrates fingerprint comparison and DCoreReplicaAdapter invokes semantic localization

claims.statement: The product provides a two-instance reference synchronization flow over real UDP loopback transport.
claims.scope: single-authority correction, x86_64 campaign, UDP loopback reference; remote production transport, multiwriter ordering and consensus are out of scope

claims.statement: Canonical SHA-256, Merkle roots, inclusion proofs and chained evidence are implemented and verified in the declared corpus.
claims.scope: GCC/Clang Linux x86_64 corpus

claims.statement: A production asymmetric State Signature provider is included.
claims.scope: interfaces exist; no concrete asymmetric provider

claims.statement: Support bundles are integrity-checked and independently verifiable.
claims.scope: bundle integrity and tamper detection; confidentiality not included

claims.statement: An installable C Host SDK provides opaque-handle lifecycle and selected runtime capabilities.
claims.scope: static library; Linux x86_64 GCC/Clang installation test

claims.statement: The full numerical pipeline is globally certified for containment and overflow.
claims.scope: rejected in CS011; only checked Q32.32 primitives and explicitly scoped solver evidence may be claimed

claims.statement: The NeoEng D-Core is ready for unrestricted production use in mission-critical sectors.
claims.scope: internal gaps, native qualification and external assurance remain

claims.statement: The horizontal D-Core can be adapted to games, simulation, robotics, digital twins, defense, aerospace and finance.
claims.scope: architectural applicability only; sector adapters and certifications are separate

claims.statement: The product demonstrably reduces engineering cost or incident resolution by the percentages in historical commercial material.
claims.scope: no customer study or independent benchmark currently supports those percentages

claims.statement: The product is certified under ISO 27001, SOC 2, IEC 61508, ISO 26262 or DO-178C.
claims.scope: certifications are future external assurance
